accepted_examples.german: Tom hat bei der Klausur in Geschichte geschummelt.
accepted_examples.english: Tom cheated on the history exam.
accepted_examples.note: Geschichte is used in the history subject sense.

accepted_examples.german: Dies ist weder die Zeit noch der Ort.
accepted_examples.english: This isn't the time or the place.
accepted_examples.note: Ort means place/location in this sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Er fährt manchmal mit dem Auto zur Arbeit.
accepted_examples.english: He sometimes goes to work by car.

accepted_examples.german: Wo wart ihr zwischen ein und drei Uhr?
accepted_examples.english: Where were you between one and three o'clock?
accepted_examples.note: zwischen expresses the time interval between one and three.

accepted_examples.german: Die Eltern spielen ein Spiel mit ihren Kindern.
accepted_examples.english: The parents are playing a game with their children.
accepted_examples.note: Spiel means a game in this example.

accepted_examples.german: Tom flehte Mary um eine andere Chance an.
accepted_examples.english: Tom begged Mary for another chance.
accepted_examples.note: Chance means an opportunity in this context.

accepted_examples.german: Es ist wichtig, viele Bücher zu lesen.
accepted_examples.english: It's important to read a lot of books.
accepted_examples.note: wichtig means important; the translation conveys the same clause.

accepted_examples.german: Er hat von uns allen am wenigsten Geld.
accepted_examples.english: He has the least money of us all.
accepted_examples.note: allen is an inflected form meaning all of us in the dative phrase von uns allen.

accepted_examples.german: Das ist das Bett, in dem Tom schläft.
accepted_examples.english: This is the bed that Tom sleeps in.
accepted_examples.note: Bett means bed in the example.
schlecht has the intended poor/bad-quality sense here.

accepted_examples.german: Heutzutage lernen die Kinder in der Schule schwimmen.
accepted_examples.english: Nowadays, children learn to swim in school.
accepted_examples.note: Schule means school in this sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Denkt ihr nicht, dass ich eine Entschuldigung verdiene?
accepted_examples.english: Don't you think I deserve an apology?
accepted_examples.note: Entschuldigung means apology in this context.

accepted_examples.german: Soweit ich weiß, gibt es kein solches Wort.
accepted_examples.english: As far as I know, there is no such word.

accepted_examples.german: Tom machte die Augen zu und schlief ein.
accepted_examples.english: Tom closed his eyes and fell asleep.
accepted_examples.note: schlief is a past-tense form of schlafen, used in the literal sleep sense.

accepted_examples.german: Tom wusch sich die Hände und das Gesicht.
accepted_examples.english: Tom washed his hands and face.
accepted_examples.note: Gesicht means face in this sentence.

entry_updates.value: all (inflected form of alle; dative plural here)
entry_updates.note: Corrected the incorrect genitive-singular gloss; allen is an inflected form and the example uses dative plural von uns allen.

plural_reviews.note: Götter is the plural for individual deities; the monotheistic sense is normally singular-only.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Götter for multiple deities. In the monotheistic sense, Gott has no plural.

plural_reviews.note: The time-point sense has plural Momente.
Jungen is standard; Jungens and Jungs are colloquial regional alternatives.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Standard plural: Jungen. Jungens and Jungs are colloquial, especially regional alternatives.

plural_reviews.note: Duden lists Musiken but marks plural use rare and the everyday music-as-sound sense as without plural.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Musik is normally uncountable in the everyday sense. Duden lists the rare plural Musiken; do not treat it as the ordinary plural for music generally.

plural_reviews.note: Fälle is correct for cases/instances; the act of falling is often singular-only.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Fälle for cases or instances. The meaning 'the act of falling' is usually singular-only.

plural_reviews.note: Duden gives Babys as the plural for infants.
Dinge is the standard plural; Dinger is colloquial and sense-restricted.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Dinge is the usual plural. Dinger is colloquial, especially for unspecified objects or people described dismissively.

plural_reviews.note: Orte is the ordinary plural; Örter is limited to nautical, mathematical and related technical usage.
plural_reviews.usage_note: Use Orte for everyday places. Örter is a technical alternative, especially in nautical or mathematical contexts.

plural_reviews.note: Duden marks the euphemistic menstruation sense of Tage as plural-only.
Typen is the plural for the category/person senses.
Gesichter is the plural for faces and people described as familiar or unfamiliar faces.
Teile is the plural for parts or pieces.
Herzen is the standard plural for the organ, feeling and heart-shaped object senses; playing-card suit has a separate use.
plural_reviews.usage_note: The ordinary plural is Herzen. For the card suit, Duden also records a separate plural use Herz.

plural_reviews.note: Pläne is the plural for plans or projects.
